transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, honestly, it's... it's mostly physical. My neck and shoulders are just... they're tight all the time now. My jaw, too. It's like I'm... I don't know, bracing for bad news, I guess. Even when I'm just sitting at my desk at school, or trying to watch TV at night. It's just constant. So... I figured I should come in.
Is the tightness in your neck, shoulders, and jaw painful?
Yeah. It's... it aches. Like I said, it's just that it's tight all the time. When you're constantly bracing like that... it gets pretty sore.
Is the ache in your neck, shoulders, and jaw always there, or does it come and go?
Like I said... it's pretty much almost all the time. It doesn't really let up.
Do you think your neck, shoulder, and jaw tightness is related to how you're feeling emotionally?
I don't know. I mean... maybe? I just know it hurts. I haven't really thought about it like that.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or emotional state around the same time your neck, shoulder, and jaw tightness started?

I guess... I don't know if it's a mood thing, exactly. It's just... my mind doesn't really stop. It's always jumping around. Like, I'll be worrying if the contractors missed something fixing up the house, and then I'm thinking about work... wondering if my lesson plans are slipping, or if the robotics club kids are falling behind. And then... I don't know, I just worry I'm disappointing my wife and the family because I can't seem to keep a handle on everything. It's just... a lot of that. All the time.
Do you think your worries are worse than what might be expected for the situations you're dealing with?
I don't know. I mean... maybe? It just feels like... like a lot to deal with. I haven't really thought about if it's worse than it should be. It's just how it is.
Do you think you worry more about these things than other people would in your situation?
I'm not sure. I haven't really... asked anyone else how they'd handle it. I just know it's what's going on in my head.
Do you think your worries are keeping you from doing things you want or need to do?

I suppose so. I mean... I'm a bit behind on my lesson prep and grading lately. And... well, I usually help manage the community theater, but I had to step back from some of that. I just... couldn't keep up with it all.
Are you able to stop worrying when you want to?

Not really. I mean... I try. I'll tell myself to just stop and focus on the class in front of me. But... it doesn't really work. Just one little thing pops into my head—like a late invoice, or a student who's falling behind—and it just sets off this whole chain of what-ifs. I can't really... shut it down once it starts.
Do you feel like your worrying is causing you a lot of distress?
I guess so. It's... tiring. Just having it there all the time.
Are you having trouble with your relationships with family or friends because of your worrying or physical symptoms?
I don't think so. I mean... my wife notices I'm stressed, but we get along fine. I don't really talk about it much with friends. We just... do our normal things.
Have you had to take any days off from work or school because of your worrying or physical symptoms?

No, I haven't taken any days off. I still go in. But... I suppose I've been falling behind a bit. Just on things like lesson prep, and... grading. And I did have to step back from some of the community-theater work I usually manage. I just... I couldn't really keep up with all of it anymore.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but have stopped doing because of your worrying or physical symptoms?

I mean, I just mentioned the theater stuff. I used to do a lot more with the community group, managing things... but I had to give a lot of that up. And like I said, the school work... the grading and prep... I just can't seem to stay on top of it like I used to.
Do you worry about things even when everything in your life seems to be going well?
I suppose so. It just... the worrying is kind of always there, regardless.
Are your worries mostly about one area of your life or are they spread across many different areas?

It's... it's a lot of things, I suppose. It's not just one area. I, um... I worry about the house, if the contractors missed something. And then my mind just jumps to work... the lesson plans slipping, the robotics kids falling behind. And then... I don't know, just whether I'm disappointing my wife and family because I can't seem to keep it all under control. It just spreads out.
Do you find it difficult to push these worries out of your mind when they come up?

I guess so. I mean... I can tell myself to stop. Try to just focus on the class right in front of me. But... it doesn't really work. One small thought, like... an unpaid invoice for the house, or a kid struggling... it just starts this whole chain of what-ifs. And... I just can't seem to shut it down once it starts.
Have you noticed any significant problems at work or at home because of your worrying?

I don't know if I'd call it significant, but... I suppose things are slipping a bit. I've been falling behind on my lesson prep... and the grading. And I, um... I usually help manage some community theater work, but I had to give parts of that up recently. I just couldn't keep up with it all anymore.
Are there any areas of your life where you don't worry about things?
I... I don't really think so. Not that I can think of, anyway. It just sort of... follows me around, I guess.
Do you think that your worries about your physical symptoms, like the neck and shoulder tightness, are disproportionate to the actual problems they cause?
I don't know. I mean... I guess I hadn't really thought about it like that. It just... it hurts, you know? So I worry about it.
